contributions.statement: Beside the schema or compile gate on agent-generated structured artifacts (OpenAPI files, config, migration plans, generated workflows), add a check that rejects degenerate outputs, such as artifacts with no substantive action or step nodes or bodies that only declare a capability 'unavailable', because a model can decline the task in a schema-valid form and push the structural pass rate up while task satisfaction collapses.
contributions.evidence: §VI-D, Tables III and V: on v2, gpt-oss-120b has the highest structural success of any cell (97.8%, 227/232) but the lowest majority-vote satisfaction (6.9% of 29 prompts, down from 24.1% on v1; mean 58.9 to 44.9, SE 2.9/2.1). The judge's rationales attribute this to single-comment stub workflows declaring integrations unavailable. Stubs were not counted directly, and the judge is unvalidated.
relative_to: 2609.22222 schema-matched / executable answers silently wrong about one in five
2605.27531 reject trivially-true agent contracts as a separate gate check

contributions.statement: When you change a fixed agent pipeline (prompt structure, staging, retrieval), re-qualify every model you route to on both a structural and a task-level check, because the same change that helped most models cut one model's task score by 14 points and another's output rate by about 14 points.
contributions.evidence: Tables II-V, same 29 prompts, 8 runs each, same infrastructure: v2 raised structural success for all six models, but gpt-oss-120b's semantic mean fell 58.9 to 44.9 (SE 2.9/2.1) and llama-3.3-70b's generation rate fell 95.3% to 81.5% (221 to 189 of 232). The llama drop is unexplained by the authors.
relative_to: 2609.32459 re-measure harness components at each model upgrade
2605.17535 multi-stage pipeline helps only the weakest model

contributions.statement: For a structured artifact that mid-size models fail to emit in one call, generate it in fixed stages (scaffold, then top-level parts, then nested parts) behind a deterministic validator, a programmatic fix and a bounded (2-attempt) LLM patch loop, and budget for 2.4-4x the input tokens and +8-75 s latency.
contributions.evidence: §III-B, Tables II-IV: structural success rose from 31.5-82.8% to 74.1-97.8% for all six models, but the staging was changed together with planner placement, plan revision and new retrieval sources, with no ablation.
relative_to: 2605.15425 deterministic orchestration with narrow schema-validated LLM calls; fine-grained decomposition triples tokens
2607.01980 JSON schema plus deterministic validator for generated artifacts

reason: Two moderate refinements survive, both about gates and qualification rather than about graphs. A schema gate needs a degenerate-output check because a model can decline in a schema-valid form, here at 97.8% structural against 6.9% satisfied. A fixed pipeline change must be re-qualified per model because it helped five models and broke one. The staged-generation recipe stays weak: it is confounded with new retrieval sources and has no agent-loop or same-budget baseline.
